format: InfinityDB expanded non-catalog battlefield element reviews
scope: audit-only; excludes publication, inferred object profiles, carriers and delivery

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Marker is a game element with Attributes represented by a Marker
reviews.caveat: The glossary describes an on-table representation, not a concrete new Weapon/Equipment profile. Resolve the represented source element separately.

factsEvidence: Place one Console at the center of each of the four scoring Quadrants
Represent each Console with a Console A Marker or scenery of the same diameter.
reviews.caveat: The four Console objectives are Domination scenario elements represented by markers or scenery, not catalog Weapon/Equipment Deployables. Maintain scenario geometry and Hack Consoles separately.

factsEvidence: Place three Supply Boxes: one at the center of the table
Represent each Supply Box with a Supply Box Marker or a similar scenery item.
reviews.caveat: The three Supply Boxes are Supplies scenario objectives, not Army-carried Weapon/Equipment object identities. Their placement and carrying restrictions are scenario scoped.

factsEvidence: At game end, a player controls a Supply Box only if one of their Models is carrying it.
reviews.caveat: Controlling a scenario Supply Box does not create another object identity; it only defines when an existing objective scores.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Short Skill used by Specialist Troops to Hack a Console.
factsEvidence: The Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with a Console.
A successful unopposed [[attribute:wip]] Roll Hacks the Console.
reviews.caveat: Hack Consoles changes the state/owner of an existing scenario Console; it creates no new console or Army equipment delivery edge.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Activate Disco Ball is a Short Skill (Attack) for reactivating a deployed allied Disco Ball.
factsEvidence: The deployed Disco Ball must be allied and in LoF or [[trait:zone-of-control-zc|Zone of Control]].
An enemy Disco Ball cannot be activated.
reviews.caveat: Activate Disco Ball interacts with the already reviewed Disco Baller source-mode deployed Disco Ball. It does not introduce a second source Weapon, new Ball identity, or another placement path.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Deployment Skill that lets the user deploy with false replicas represented through [[state:decoy]].
factsEvidence: When placed on the table, the user may deploy in [[state:decoy]].
reviews.caveat: Decoy lets a Trooper deploy with false replicas. These are representations associated with that Trooper, not separate Weapon/Equipment profiles or Army carriers.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Marker State created by [[equipment:holoprojector]] that conceals which of up to three representations is the real bearer.
factsEvidence: A holographic duplicate disappears separately when Discovered, entering enemy Silhouette contact, being hit by a successful Attack (no Saving Roll), or breaking Coherency.
reviews.caveat: Holoecho replicas belong to one Holoprojector bearer, not to separate Army Unit or Weapon/Equipment identities. N5.3 p. 162 specifies that replicas can provoke AROs and trigger Mines or CrazyKoalas; they are not inert decorations. P. 163 describes cancellation.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A deployment state in which a Trooper's position is recorded privately without placing a Model or Marker on the table.
factsEvidence: The Trooper is not placed on the table while the state is active and is generally treated as not being on the table.
reviews.caveat: Hidden Deployment records an existing Trooper's position privately. Revealing that Trooper places the same Model or Marker; it does not create another object or source ownership.

reviews.summaryEvidence: The stronger Impersonation Marker State, which represents the user as an apparent ally
factsEvidence: The Model is replaced by an IMP-1 Marker and enemies perceive it as Allied.
A normal successful [[skill:discover]] Roll against IMP-1 applies the State's WIP -3 MOD and changes the user to [[state:impersonation-2]].
reviews.caveat: The IMP-1 Marker represents an existing disguised Trooper, not an independent deployed device. A normal successful Discover changes IMP-1 to IMP-2 rather than directly revealing the Model.

reviews.summaryEvidence: The second Impersonation Marker State, which disguises the user until a successful [[skill:discover]] Roll reveals the Model.
factsEvidence: The Model is replaced by an IMP-2 Marker and enemies perceive it as Allied.
A successful [[skill:discover]] Roll removes IMP-2 and replaces the Marker with the corresponding Model.
reviews.caveat: IMP-2 represents the existing disguised Trooper, not a new Weapon/Equipment identity. A successful Discover reveals the Model; this differs from IMP-1's normal downgrade to IMP-2.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Common Skill used to reveal game elements represented by Markers.
factsEvidence: The user must be able to draw LoF to the target Marker.
The user makes the required WIP Roll to reveal an eligible Marker.
reviews.caveat: Discover reveals an already represented Trooper, Weapon or Equipment; the original entity and Marker State determine identity and resolution. It does not create a new game object.

reviews.summaryEvidence: An Automatic Special Skill that imposes its listed negative MOD on targets' Face to Face ARO Rolls
factsEvidence: The user must begin the Order in Marker form or [[state:hidden-deployment|Hidden Deployment]].
The Attack imposes the negative Surprise Attack MOD shown in the Unit Profile
reviews.caveat: Surprise Attack modifies an existing Trooper's Attack when starting in Marker or Hidden Deployment. Marker use does not establish another object or source Weapon.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Short Special Skill that detects hidden threats in the user's Zone of Control
factsEvidence: The user may make a Normal WIP+6 Roll to simultaneously [[skill:discover]] enemy Troopers, Weapons, or Equipment
The user gains +6 WIP when declaring [[skill:discover]] against Camouflage Markers.
reviews.caveat: Sensor can detect and reveal existing hidden Troopers, Weapons or Equipment, not place new ones. Preserve each revealed element's independently sourced identity.
